title: Check if Every Row and Column Contains All Numbers
statement:
You are given a square integer grid `matrix` of size `n x n`. The grid counts as *valid* when each of its rows, and each of its columns, includes every integer `1, 2, ..., n`.

Return `true` if `matrix` is valid and `false` if it is not.
notes:
## Intuition

Every value already lies between `1` and `n`, and a row holds exactly `n` values. So a row contains all of `1..n` exactly when its `n` values are all different, and the same goes for a column. Checking "all different" is a job for a hash set: add every value and compare the set's size with `n`.

The brute force asks, for each number `1..n`, whether it appears in each row and column, which costs O(n³). The set turns each line into a single O(n) pass.

## Approach

1. Let `n` be the side length.
2. For each index `i`, make two empty sets: `rowSeen` for row `i` and `colSeen` for column `i`.
3. For each `j`, add `matrix[i][j]` to `rowSeen` and `matrix[j][i]` to `colSeen`.
4. If either set ended up smaller than `n`, some value repeated, so some number is missing: return `false`.
5. If every row and column passed, return `true`.

## Example 1, step by step

`matrix = [[1,2,3],[3,1,2],[2,3,1]]`, `n = 3`. For `i = 0`, `rowSeen = {1,2,3}` and column 0 gives `colSeen = {1,3,2}`; both have size 3. For `i = 1`, row `{3,1,2}` and column `{2,1,3}`; for `i = 2`, row `{2,3,1}` and column `{3,2,1}`. All sizes are 3, so the answer is `true`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n²): each cell is added to one row set and one column set.
- Space: O(n) for the two sets of the current index.

## Pitfalls

- Checking only the rows (or only the columns) misses grids like `[[1,2],[1,2]]`.
- The size test is enough only because every value is in `1..n`; without that guarantee you would also have to check the range.
- Use fresh sets for every `i`; reusing them across rows mixes lines together.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | the grid's side length |
| `i` | the row index, and also the column index being checked |
| `j` | position inside that row and column |
| `rowSeen` | distinct values in row `i` |
| `colSeen` | distinct values in column `i` |

narration.2: n is the side length, and also the largest value that should appear.
narration.3: Index i picks both row i and column i to check together.
narration.4: rowSeen collects the distinct values of row i.
narration.5: colSeen collects the distinct values of column i.
narration.7: Add the value in row i, column j to the row set.
narration.8: Add the value in row j, column i to the column set.
narration.10: Fewer than n distinct values means a repeat, so some number from 1 to n is missing.
narration.11: That line is incomplete, so the matrix is not valid.
narration.14: Every row and column held n different values, so the matrix is valid.
